{{Otheruses|Kessel}}
The '''Hoersch-Kessel ion drive''' was a popular [[Sublight engine/Legends|sublight drive]] developed and manufactured by [[Hoersch-Kessel Drive, Inc./Legends|Hoersch-Kessel Drive, Inc.]]. The design was introduced to [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]]<ref name="SWS">''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]''</ref> thousands of [[Standard year/Legends|years]] before the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]<ref name="TRG2">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'', Second Edition]]</ref> by [[Alien/Legends|alien]] [[Merchant/Legends|merchants]]. The design was prevalent throughout the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], and most [[starshipwright]]s included Hoersch-Kessel-style motors into their products.<ref name="SWS" />

The drive created a fusion reaction that broke down the fuel into charged particles<ref name="SWS" /> known as ions<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|48|Hoersch-Kessel ion drive}}</ref> to drive [[Starship/Legends|starships]] through [[Realspace/Legends|realspace]]. The energy generated by the reaction created thrust which propelled the ship. Directional movement was attained by the use of [[Baffle (component)/Legends|baffles]] or [[Vectral/Legends|vectrals]], or by smaller [[lateral thruster]]s on smaller vessels.<ref name="SWS" />

The Hoersch-Kessel could operate on virtually any type of fuel; while [[Uranium/Legends|uranium]] or similar heavy metals were preferred, the drive could be easily modified to accept liquid reactants, [[energy conversion cell]]s, or [[ion-collector pod]]s as a replacement fuel source. The design was also highly adaptable, being able to be scaled down to fit in a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]], or enlarged to work on a [[Capital ship/Legends|capital ship]]. The design's common nature meant that repairing the drive was easy, as most [[Technician/Legends|technicians]] were intimately familiar with the workings of a Hoersch-Kessel ion drive. Replacement parts were also commonly stocked throughout the galaxy, although the drive featured few moving parts. Maintenance of the Hoersch-Kessel was essential, as the engine intake and [[firing cell]]s were required to be in precise alignment, and the unit had to be tuned up regularly.<ref name="SWS" />

The exhaust from the Hoersch-Kessel was hot and slightly [[Radiation/Legends|radioactive]], but was safe to use within the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] of an inhabited [[Planet/Legends|planet]]. The emissions were shielded using [[collector coil]]s which were routinely scrubbed and replaced during maintenance. Maintenance personnel carrying out works on a Hoersch-Kessel usually wore radiation-proof garments and took regular [[anti-radiation inoculation]]s.<ref name="SWS2">[[The Star Wars Sourcebook (Second Edition)|''The Star Wars Sourcebook'', Second Edition]]</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
In [[1987]]'s ''[[The Star Wars Sourcebook]]'' by [[West End Games]], it was stated that use of a Hoersch-Kessel ion drive in the atmosphere of an inhabited planet was illegal due to the radioactive nature of the exhaust. When the book was reprinted in [[1994]], updated for the [[The Star Wars Sourcebook (Second Edition)|Second Edition]] rules, this fact was removed from the description of the Hoersch-Kessel, and it was explicitly stated that the drive was safe to use in an atmosphere.
